title: Smart Water Valve with Automatic Shut-Off, Leak Detection, and Home-Wide Monitoring
summary: This Old House’s This Old House segment documents a smart water valve system designed to automatically shut off water supply on detection of abnormal flow or leaks, with a network of sensors (flow, pressure, and temperature) and a Wi‑Fi-enabled app. The video explains how the main-line flow sensor governs the automatic shut-off valve, how pressure and temperature sensors help prevent pipe bursts in cold environments, and how the app dashboard tracks real-time usage, provides a conservation goal, and supports troubleshooting when leaks appear. The presenters demonstrate immediate valve actuation, data visualization of usage by category (irrigation, showers, etc.), and a “health test” that can detect small drips, along with the potential for future device integrations with smart thermostats to further protect the home’s plumbing system."
topics: water usage by category (irrigation, showers, etc.)
comparing market options for shut-off sensors
habits learning in smart water systems

sections.title: System concept and team introduction
concepts: team background (plumbing and legal claims experience)
objective to prevent catastrophic water damage
sections.description: Gabe and Ross introduce the goal of the project: a smart automatic water shut-off valve that can prevent major water damage by combining a valve with leak-detection sensors and data analytics.

sections.title: Main-line flow sensor and automatic shut-off
sections.description: Explanation of the main flow sensor mounted on the water supply line and how detected abnormal flow can trigger the valve to shut off water to prevent further damage.

sections.title: Additional sensing: pressure and temperature
sections.description: Introduction of the pressure and temperature sensors, highlighting their roles in detecting high pressure, aging piping, and freezing conditions that can cause bursts.

sections.title: Wi‑Fi connectivity and remote alerts
sections.description: Discussion of how the device communicates via Wi‑Fi to alert the user and aid in troubleshooting when leaks are detected.

sections.title: Dashboard, usage history, and conservation goals
sections.description: Showcase of the dashboard that tracks today’s water usage, the homeowner’s conservation goal, and a learned history of how water is used (noting irrigation as a major use, followed by showers).

sections.title: Leak health test and drip detection
sections.description: Demonstration of a health test capable of detecting a small drip and providing troubleshooting steps within the app to locate leaks.

sections.title: Future integrations and smart-home safety
sections.description: Discussion of plans for devices to communicate with each other, including potential thermostat-triggered actions to prevent pipe freezing and improve overall safety.

sections.title: Market context and closing reflections
sections.description: Overall reflections on the range of similar devices on the market, the trade-off between nuisance alarms and actual leaks, and the value of measuring and learning from water usage to reduce catastrophic damage.
